title: A two-piano record with Tommy Flanagan
summary: Basie calls Flanagan the most underrated pianist but says Tommy scares you; he had never thought about recording with him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Sure. Of course. Absolutely. Could you see doing a record like you did with Pete -- could you see doing it, say, with Tommy Flanagan, the two of you?

To tell you the truth, I have kind of [pianist] different feelings altogether. We haven't really did anything together. I mean we did a couple things -- Pete and I did a couple things, but we just (inaudible), you know. But Tommy and I haven't been that close. And I love him, you know. Right in the number one slot as far as I'm concerned. As I said before, I think he's the most underrated pianist around.
But Tommy -- man, I'm telling you, Tommy scares you.
Well, why couldn't you two do a thing? Two different kinds of standards?
Never thought about it at all.
Why don't you think about it.
let you Norman should do it?
